entry.title: IceCube Nobel Prize
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Francis Halzen was awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for his decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, according to CERN Courier. Separately, IceCube reports that its outgoing South Pole winterovers have been succeeded by two new ones, Justin and Dane, who arrived at the Pole this week.

entry.title: DUNE cryostats
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Crews from Fermilab, CERN and SURF have started building the first of two cryostats for DUNE. These are large insulated containers designed to hold liquid argon at very low temperature, and together they will house approximately 17,000 tons of it. The work is taking place nearly a mile underground in South Dakota, where crews are assembling large steel beams to form the outer structure of the detector modules.

entry.title: Super-Kamiokande solar neutrinos
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A new analysis uses Super-Kamiokande phase I-IV data, covering 5805 days, to study 8B solar neutrinos. It presents an outer bound on the size of the solar core and measurements of the density and temperature in the core. The inference rests on the sensitivity of the 8B production rate to core temperature and on the dependence of adiabatic flavour conversion on the local electron density.

entry.title: PTOLEMY RF tracker
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. PTOLEMY aims to measure the neutrino mass from the tritium endpoint and, in the future, to detect the Cosmic Neutrino Background. A new paper describes the design, simulation, construction and commissioning of the Electron Trap, a prototype of the RF Tracker. The RF Tracker is a sub-detector intended to measure electrons in real time by cyclotron radiation emission spectroscopy, and the paper presents measurements and data analysis from the prototype.

entry.title: Warwick gas TPC
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Active-target gas time projection chambers could provide the measurements of neutrino interactions needed for future oscillation measurements. A new paper presents the construction and commissioning of WarTPC, an R&D platform that operates at pressures up to approximately 10 bar. It combines thick gas electron multipliers with a Timepix3 camera for optical readout.

entry.title: Reactor antineutrino background
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A simulation study uses a multilayer perceptron trained on topological observables from Geant4 simulations to suppress correlated fast-neutron background in segmented reactor antineutrino detectors. In shallow or above-ground scintillator detectors this background is dominant, because proton recoils can mimic the prompt inverse-beta-decay signal. The Indian Scintillator Matrix for Reactor Anti-Neutrinos detector is used as the case study, and the paper also addresses sterile-neutrino sensitivity.

entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper investigates the contribution of Δ-direct-Urca processes to neutrino emissivity in neutron stars that may contain Δ isobars. Its authors state that this contribution had not been explicitly evaluated before. It matters to neutrino physicists because these processes enter the neutrino cooling of dense stellar matter.

entry.title: The authors study how well kiloton-scale detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande could determine the primary cosmic
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors study how well kiloton-scale detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande could determine the primary cosmic-ray spectrum from the atmospheric neutrino flux. They report that future detectors can distinguish between cosmic-ray models with high statistical significance, even allowing for uncertainties in cross sections and hadronic interactions. This links atmospheric neutrino measurements to the cosmic-ray inputs on which flux predictions depend.

entry.title: Motivated by updated IceCube data on NGC 1068 down to about 0.2 TeV, the paper performs a model-independent in
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Motivated by updated IceCube data on NGC 1068 down to about 0.2 TeV, the paper performs a model-independent inference of the neutrino production conditions near the supermassive black hole. It computes hadronic neutrino production and accompanying cascade gamma rays, and explores the parameter space with Latin hypercube sampling under multimessenger constraints. It is relevant as a quantitative attempt to say what physical conditions the first identified extragalactic neutrino source requires.

entry.title: The paper proves a no-go theorem: any completely positive trace-preserving evolution covariant under rotations
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper proves a no-go theorem: any completely positive trace-preserving evolution covariant under rotations of the mass-coherence plane is exactly blind to a Majorana phase in open two-flavour oscillations. It also identifies when a rate anisotropy in the environment can supply the phase reference needed to make the phase visible. This sets a clear condition for when decoherence could reveal the Dirac or Majorana nature of neutrinos.

entry.title: The authors derive semianalytic approximations for the outcomes of slow and fast flavour conversion in quasiho
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors derive semianalytic approximations for the outcomes of slow and fast flavour conversion in quasihomogeneous neutrino ensembles, as a subgrid scheme for supernova simulations that cannot include neutrino quantum kinetics. They report excellent agreement with multiangle and multienergy solutions of the kinetic equations, independent of the mass ordering. This is useful for including self-interaction effects in core-collapse modelling.

entry.title: The paper studies thermal leptogenesis in the Babu-Nandi-Tavartkiladze model, in which neutrino masses arise f
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper studies thermal leptogenesis in the Babu-Nandi-Tavartkiladze model, in which neutrino masses arise from a dimension-7 operator at tree level and a dimension-5 operator at one loop. The model accommodates sub-eV neutrino masses with new physics at the TeV scale. Its leptogenesis differs from the canonical seesaw case, which makes it a testable alternative.
